title: Declarations, definitions and calls
goal: Trace the prototype, call and return of a numerical function.

prerequisites.text: Validate two integers and understand return.

terms.title: Declaration
terms.definition: Associates the name with the function type. A prototype also specifies the parameter types.

terms.title: Definition
terms.definition: Contains the body executed at a call.

terms.title: Argument
terms.definition: An expression supplying a value to a parameter.

sections.title: Why it matters
paragraphs: Before calculating a floor area, a carpenter specifies the measurements needed. A prototype states a similar contract: name, return type and parameters.
A prototype ends at its semicolon. A definition contains a body. A prototype makes a later definition callable from main.
In C17, the prototype int f(void) specifies a function with no parameters. The declaration int f() leaves the parameters unspecified.
A prototype lets the compiler check the shape of a call. A separate example checks the calculation itself: a valid call with two integers may still return the wrong area.

sections.title: Worked example
paragraphs: Predict rect_area(3, 4) and locate the declaration, call and definition in the source.
steps: Before call → 3, 4 → parameters → Enter the body
In the body → 3 × 4 → 12 → return sends a value

sections.title: Diagnostics
paragraphs: A prototype detects a missing argument at compile time. Count the expressions at the call site and compare them with the parameters.
A file with a declaration may compile without a definition. Building an executable also needs the definition at link time.

sections.title: Transfer to practice
paragraphs: Separate calculation from input for shelf cells too. Zero rows give zero capacity even when each row has positive capacity.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Trace the prototype, call and return of a numerical function.

feedback: The body runs on a call.

selfcheck.prompt: What can the compiler catch in a call with one number?
feedback: Match the call to the prototype.
The row count is not checked here.

selfcheck.prompt: Why is the call valid when its body is below main?
selfcheck.feedback: The compiler saw the prototype before the call. At runtime the call enters the body and receives an int.

diagnosticExercises.source:
static int cells(int rows, int count) { return rows * count; }
int main(void) { return cells(2); }

practice.title: Cells in a shelf section
practice.task: Read rows and cells per row on separate lines, from 0 to 50. Keep the slot_count declaration, call and definition. Repair its calculation. Print the cell count or invalid. The supplied read_integer function checks the first two lines. A missing line, an invalid number or an out-of-range value gives invalid. The program ignores any later input.
practice.hint: Compare addition and multiplication when there are zero rows.
criteria: slot_count calculates while main reads and prints.
Invalid data is rejected before calculation.

steps.action: Enter 2 and 6 on separate lines, then run the starter.
steps.why: Trace the prototype, call and return of a numerical function.
steps.expected: The starter adds the numbers and prints 8. The requirement calls for 12.

steps.action: Fix the calculation in slot_count. Compare the results for 2 and 6, then for 0 and 6.
steps.why: The change must satisfy the contract.
steps.expected: The corrected program prints 12 and 0 respectively.

steps.action: Check a distinct boundary case and explain the result.
steps.why: Different cases distinguish the parts of the rule.
steps.expected: Invalid data is rejected before calculation.

exercises.title: Independent transfer
exercises.task: Move the definition above main in a copy and remove the separate prototype. Explain why the test still prints 12.
criteria: The definition is visible when the call is checked.

teaching.scene: A carpenter needs to verify the area calculation independently of printing. Trace both dimensions into the parameters and follow the result back to the call.

predict.prompt: main calls rect_area(3, 4). Which values do the two parameters receive, what comes back, and what reaches stdout?
predict.answer: width receives 3 and height receives 4. The body multiplies them and returns 12. main stores the result in floor, and a separate printf writes 12.

apply.prompt: For a 2 by 5 panel, which pair would you pass and which value should the same contract return?
apply.answer: Pass 2 and 5 in width and height order. The call should return 10. Compare that value directly with the calculated area.

practice.strategy: Keep the declaration and calls consistent. State how rows and cells per row combine, then check ordinary and zero dimensions.
practice.diagnosis: If two rows of six give 8, both the call and output happened. Compare the calculation with the number of cells in two equal rows.

syntax.explanation: The prototype gives the result and parameter types before the call. The definition has the corresponding signature, a body and return.
syntax.mistake: The types and number of parameters must agree in the prototype and definition. Check the signatures first when they differ.
